evidence: Ov. Am. 1.6.7: lēniter īre per excubiās custōdum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of movement, speech and heat alike; of a slope, gradually (collis lēniter acclīvis, Caes. B.G. 7.19).

evidence: Plaut. Ps. 5.2.7: molliter sustinē mē (Lewis & Short)
Cic. N.D. 2.129: avēs nīdōs mollissimē substernunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of touch and handling: softly, so as not to hurt or break.
Said on its own to someone rushing: placidē!, gently, easy now.

phrases.latin: in focō caldō sub testū coquitō lēniter
phrases.english: bake it gently on a hot hearth under a crock

phrases.latin: quasi admīrāns stetit ac deinde sēnsim atque placidē, tamquam nōscitābundus, ad hominem accēdit
phrases.english: he stopped as if amazed, and then slowly and gently, as though recognising him, came up to the man
